topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
consensus_response: A 0.25 dB passband loss reduces signal power, increasing required transmitter power and interference susceptibility. This necessitates an increase in transmitter power to maintain a given link margin, but also increases noise and interference susceptibility. The reduced signal power due to the 0.25 dB passband loss compromises network capacity and reliability by increasing the required transmission time and reducing the available bandwidth for the desired signal. As a result, the system's ability to maintain a given data rate would be impaired, ultimately affecting the overall network performance.
